## You must change `docs/ or tests/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [docs/ or tests/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
docs/GRAMMAR.md:129-155 documents a whole static type system in '## 2. Type System' / '### 2.1 Type Expressions' - `type_expression`, `primitive_type`, `list_type`, `record_type`, `object_type`, `function_type`, `generic_type`, `union_type` - and then USES it in five productions that carry no disclaimer: :188 `declaration = 'set' identifier [ ':' type_expression ] 'to' expression`, :194 the same for `constant`, :289-290 `function_decl` with `[ 'needs' type_expression ... ]` and `[ 'gives' type_expression ]`, :294-295 `parameter = identifier [ ':' type_expression ] | identifier 'of' type_expression`, and :305 `property_decl = 'has' identifier [ ':' type_expression ] [ 'default' expression ]`. SPEC.md:147-156 repeats it under '### Complex Types' (`set numbers to list of number`, `set Point to record { x: number, y: number }`). NONE of it is implemented: verified against the built binary this audit, `set x : number to 1` raises `ParserError: Expected 'to' but got Colon`, `constant C : number to 1` the same, `object P / has x : number` raises `ParserError: Unexpected token Colon`, `to f(x : number)` raises `ParserError: Expected RightParen but got Colon`, `to f(x of number)` raises `ParserError: Expected RightParen but got Identifier("of")`, `to f(a) needs number` raises `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'needs'`, and `set numbers to list of number` raises `AnalyzerError: Unknown variable 'list'`. The project already has the honest convention and simply missed it here: docs/GRAMMAR.md:50-68 marks nine freed keywords and writes 'A reserved word the parser cannot read is not a feature', and :228-236 marks `when_statement` NOT IMPLEMENTED - but section 2 carries neither note. A reader of SPEC.md believes Redblue has types.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Make docs/GRAMMAR.md section 2 and SPEC.md's Complex Types section tell the truth: either the annotations are implemented, or every unimplemented production is marked Not Implemented and pinned by a test that fails if the marking drifts from the parser.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-113
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] every one of the five type-annotation productions (GRAMMAR.md:188, :194, :289-290, :294-295, :305) and SPEC.md:147-156 either parses, or carries a Not Implemented note in the same style as GRAMMAR.md:50-68 and :228-236
- [ ] a test asserts that every production marked Not Implemented is in fact REFUSED by the built parser, and fails if the parser starts accepting it without the note being removed
- [ ] a test asserts every keyword that appears in a GRAMMAR production as a literal (e.g. `needs`, `gives`) is listed in GRAMMAR.md:41-50 or the production is marked Not Implemented - `needs` and `gives` are currently in neither
- [ ] if annotations are implemented rather than marked, `set x : number to 1` must reject `set x : text to 1` with a positioned error, and the tests assert both directions
- [ ] edge_* tests cover: the annotation present, absent, malformed (`set x : to 1`), doubled (`set x : number : text to 1`), and on `set`/`constant`/`parameter`/`has`/function-declaration respectively
- [ ] `cargo test` reports 0 failures and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean
